text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually has no symptoms at all, which is why it is often called the "silent killer".
The Silent Nature of High Blood Pressure

list.snippet: No warning signs: Most people with high blood pressure feel completely fine and do not notice any changes.
Years of damage: The condition can quietly damage your heart, brain, and kidneys for years before it is discovered.
Regular checks needed: The only way to know your status is to get your blood pressure measured regularly by a doctor or use a home monitor.

text_blocks.snippet: Symptoms of Dangerously High Blood Pressure
When blood pressure spikes to extremely high levels (a hypertensive crisis above 180/120 mm Hg), it can cause acute physical signs:

list.snippet: Severe headaches: A sudden, intense, or persistent dull morning headache.
Vision changes: Blurry vision, double vision, or sudden loss of sight.
Shortness of breath: Getting winded easily or struggling to breathe during light activity or rest.
Chest pain: Tightness or pressure in the chest area.
Neurological signs: Dizziness, fatigue, confusion, or signs of a stroke (like facial drooping or weakness).
Other indicators: Frequent nosebleeds, pounding sensations in the ears or neck, and heart palpitations.

text_blocks.snippet: Note: Seek immediate emergency medical care (call 911) if you experience a reading over 180/120 mm Hg combined with chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, or neurological changes. You can read more about warning signs through the CDC High Blood Pressure Guide or Cleveland Clinic Hypertension Overview.
